outcome: parenting attitudes and behaviors (discipline style, sense of competence, locus of control)
cohort: A large sample of 192 parents (89.6% female, average age 40 years; 27% racial/ethnic minority) with no shared prevention indicator, participating in an employer-based program.
finding: Participants reported high satisfaction with computer-mediated parenting services, and the sample generally struggled with an internal sense of control over their children's behavior, tending towards overreactive discipline, with dysfunctional parenting practices tending to co-occur.
cross-section timing: During or after participation in the computer-mediated parenting services
